question: Build a bridge probe per entity and measure how much of it the J-lens dictionary explains.

lens.vector: v_t = (g * W_U[t]) @ J_l, unit-normalised; g = final-norm gain (1 + weight)

prompt_format: raw text, no chat template, no special tokens added
filter: keep a prompt if the first word of Qwen's greedy continuation (8 tokens) equals an accepted answer, case-insensitively
probe: mean final-token residual (block output) over kept prompts minus the mean over entities

decomposition.method: non-negative OMP, NNLS refit each step
decomposition.dictionary: unit J-lens vectors of non-special tokens whose decode has a letter

metrics: fraction of probe variance in the J-part per layer
chance level of that fraction: the same decomposition of isotropic random directions (one per probed entity per layer, seed 0)
whether the entity's own token is among its J-part atoms
deviations: J-lens vectors include the final-norm gain g (the reference omits it); g rescales dimensions unevenly, so these are the directions the lens's readout actually uses.
Added (not in the plan): the random-direction chance level for the J-part share.
Entity prompts were written by the coding agent and pass the mechanical checks in data.py; the human has not reviewed them yet.
